title: Per-head mixed-format kernel broker and staged decode pacing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Our serving runtime incurs non-trivial per-token overhead when switching execution formats mid-request (e.g., head-wise INT8 fast paths vs FP8 fallback) and during long-context prefill->decode transitions. This ticket pilots a runtime component — the 'per-head kernel broker' — which defers format selection to the earliest safe point per-attention-head and co-schedules minimal amortized unpack/dequant work across decode windows. Goals: reduce format-switch latency, keep average decode P50 within SLO for mixed-precision models, and provide telemetry to quantify amortization tradeoffs.
technical_design: Introduce a lightweight broker that holds execution intent per-attention-head: preferred_format (int8|fp8|fp16), last_evaluated_perf_score, and predicted_switch_cost.
Broker decision flow: use telemetry-hinted cost model to choose head format at prefill completion, but allow opportunistic re-evaluation during early decode tokens if confidence low.
Implement 'staged decode pacing': break decode into micro-windows (e.g., 4-8 token slices) where deferred dequant/unpack can be amortized across several heads rather than done per-head immediately.
Add a shadow-lane KV mechanism: keep a compact int8 KV shadow during prefill for heads likely to remain int8, enabling incremental promotion to FP8 only when required by accuracy heuristics.
Kernel runtime changes: expose a broker-facing API for kernel selection that returns (kernel_variant_id, prefetch_plan) and supports non-blocking prefetch of a small unpack buffer.
Introduce per-request telemetry tags: broker_decision_reason, predicted_switch_cost, amortized_unpack_bytes, and decode_window_latency_breakdown.

Fallback policy: fast-path selection must be optimistic but reversible within the next micro-window; irreversible switch penalized by recording to telemetry and triggering conservative choices next request.
Provide a config flag runtime.flags.per_head_kernel_broker to gate experiments and an opt-in scoring profile for canary runs on Dedicated pools.
Add unit tests for broker decision logic, integration tests with microbatching, and a perf harness scenario with long-context prompts to validate amortization.
Performance target: reduce median format-switch overhead per request by at least 30% and maintain decode P50 <= 1.5x baseline for mixed-precision workloads under 95th percentile load.
Design doc link and diagrams to be added to Confluence (see links).
acceptance_criteria: Broker implemented and gated behind runtime flag; can be enabled per-deployment.
End-to-end decode latency for mixed-precision test scenarios shows >=30% reduction in format-switch overhead vs baseline when broker enabled.
No regressions in token correctness for guarded eval prompt set (max 0.5% increase in generation divergence compared to full-FP16 baseline).
Telemetry exposes broker_decision_reason and amortization metrics; dashboard created with per-model breakdown.
Canary run on Dedicated pool for one week with automatic rollback rule if error rate or latency SLO breaks.
Regression and unit tests added; code reviewed and merged into main with feature flag default-off.
risks: Incorrect scoring model could over-select aggressive INT8 for accuracy-sensitive heads leading to quality regressions.
Broker adds scheduling jitter if micro-window sizes are poorly tuned, harming tail latency.
KV shadowing increases memory pressure in large-batch prefill scenarios.
Complexity of reversible switches may introduce subtle race conditions between kernel threads and the orchestration layer.
Telemetry flood risk if tags are too granular; need sampling strategy.
notes: Initial prototype implemented in a feature branch with a simple linear cost model derived from microbenchmarks (see comments).
Perf harness: used 8k-context Llama-variant with 32 heads; baseline measured on Dedicated p4d-like pool.
Early results: format-switch overhead reduced ~22% on average with naive micro-windowing; further gains expected after tuning scoring thresholds.
Memory overhead from KV shadow lanes ~3-5% in our test harness; acceptable margin but needs monitoring for larger batch sizes.
Plan: start canary on low-traffic customer-owned Dedicated cluster, gather telemetry for 72 hours, then expand.
